hypothesis: A definable Japanese customer segment has material recurring subscription-management pain.
support: About 20% report cancellation trouble; 定期購入 about 80-98k consultations a year; forgetting common in two independent surveys
contradiction: Money at risk per user modest (modal ≤¥2,000/month); segment definition and prevalence unmeasured
decision_implication: Necessary but not sufficient; cannot carry continuation alone

hypothesis: Cancellation execution, rather than tracking, is the principal residual job.
contradiction: Top-cited trouble is finding the route (46.0%); forgetting is the common pain
unknown: Frequency of hard-route cases per user
decision_implication: Reframes the product toward J1/J3, which are occupied

hypothesis: Strong free substitutes do not already solve that job.
status: Contradicted for easy routes; unresolved for hard routes
contradiction: Platform lists, guides, PFMs and 188 cover J1/J3/J6; B-class routes are self-serve
unknown: Billing-rail mix of the target segment
decision_implication: Stop condition 1 effectively triggered for digital stackers (P2)

hypothesis: Enough users are willing to grant the minimum data access.
support: MF 17.3M and Moneytree about 6.5M users link accounts
contradiction: Those users grant access to incumbents, not a startup

hypothesis: Enough users are willing to delegate cancellation.
A third party can legally and contractually cancel a meaningful subset of subscriptions.
status: Unresolved, leaning against for company agents
support: Messenger reading of the resignation-agency analogy; MOJ 2023 事件性 reasoning (other context)
contradiction: docomo family-only proxies; holder or credential terms; Art. 72 contested; 2025-26 enforcement in the analogue

hypothesis: Cancellation can be executed reliably without excessive human support.
support: B routes are short; US concierge exists
contradiction: Minute budget negative at ¥500 (tight); US lead times 2-10 business days

hypothesis: The frequency or value of cancellation is enough to support the consumer business.
contradiction: Steady state 50-67% of year 1; about 0.25 cancellations per app user cumulative at the US analogue; cancellations justify only ¥22.50-450/month
decision_implication: Stop condition 4 leaning; needs recurring value

hypothesis: A payer exists with positive unit economics.
support: C07 positive if a partner pays ≥¥5.86-18.37 per enrolled user-month
contradiction: C04 payback never; partner WTP unknown; MUFG owns Moneytree; network tooling

hypothesis: Customer acquisition and retention work despite episodic usage.
support: Intent moments exist (search for 'X 解約')
contradiction: Guides own intent; paradox; churn after the need is met

hypothesis: A compounding data, integration or trust asset can form.
contradiction: Web routes scrapeable; incumbents see charge stops; no provider APIs

hypothesis: Incumbents cannot cheaply erase the wedge before the company builds that asset.
status: Contradicted for easy routes; unresolved for hard routes
support: Hard-route human execution is costly to add
contradiction: MF could add guides in weeks; networks productising; regulation by about 2027-28

hypothesis: Japan creates a genuine initial advantage rather than extra complexity.
contradiction: Family-only proxy rules; Art. 72; scraping-based card data; competitor-owned aggregation pipes
decision_implication: Japan adds complexity more than advantage

hypothesis: The company can expand beyond cancellation without losing consumer alignment.
support: Fixed-cost review is a known adjacency
contradiction: Switching revenue comes from gaining providers (conflict); negotiation legally gated; MF already there
decision_implication: No credible expansion path that keeps alignment
